POINTWISE NEWTON FAILURE AND A LAW-LEVEL REPLACEMENT
27 October 2026. Derived from the supplied frozen scientific state.

STATUS

This is a mathematical obstruction to the unrestricted pointwise L2 Newton
interface in S3, Sections 17-18, together with a positive, finite value-query
replacement for a restricted first-order operation. It is not a lower bound
for N687, not a completed polylogarithmic Gaussian-mean sampler, and not an
externally validated or historically novel result. The supplied S1-S12 files
are unchanged; all twelve supplied hashes were checked.

The decision-changing conclusion is stronger than observing that K D_G is an
unbounded perturbation: even at an exactly Gaussian AFFINE channel, the full
pointwise linearized equation has no bounded right inverse in Gaussian L2.
Some bounded C-infinity residuals have no L2 solution. An actual uniformly
Lipschitz conservative high-frequency perturbation produces the same bad
first-order forcing. Solving only the OUTPUT-LAW equation avoids this
amplification. That change preserves positivity and exact mean preservation
through a paired-replica update; acquiring a generic corrective direction at
the required query cost remains open.

1. THE SCALAR AFFINE CHANNEL ALREADY DISCRIMINATES THE INTERFACE

Let G,Z be independent standard normal variables, 0<lambda<1, and
  a=sqrt(1-lambda^2), X=lambda G+a Z.
Thus X is exactly standard normal. This comes from the legal gradient
g(x)=lambda x, F(x)=lambda x^2/2; its canonical source Stein kernel is
K=lambda. No difficulty in sampling this particular target is asserted.

Use Gaussian divergence delta_Z=Z-partial_Z and N_Z=delta_Z partial_Z.
The S3 pointwise Newton architecture restricts a correction u to
  delta_Z J=u.
This implies E[u|G]=0 for L2-domain fields. In dimension one there is no
skew-matrix gauge left. The kernel of delta_Z in L2(gamma_Z) is zero:
distributionally its solutions are c exp(Z^2/2), which are not in L2 unless
c=0. Thus J is unique once u is specified.

At this affine channel, the exact S3 linearization is
  L(u,J)=lambda partial_G u+a partial_Z u+a J.
Substituting u=delta_Z J and using partial_Z delta_Z=N_Z+1 gives
  A J := [a(N_Z+2)+lambda delta_Z partial_G]J = -R.       (1)
This calculation includes both copies of the order-one Gaussian baseline.
The '+2' is essential.

INDEPENDENT AUDIT: THE POINTWISE NEWTON INVERSE AT AN EXACT GAUSSIAN
27 October 2026. Checks of the parent's N687 affine calculation.

RESULT. The proposed Hermite coefficients, signs, exponential norm lower bound,
and bounded-C-infinity nonexistence example are correct. This rules out a
bounded arbitrary-residual L2 right inverse for this pointwise Newton equation.
It is NOT a target sampling lower bound. The distinction between arbitrary
residuals and residuals produced by actual admissible channels remains essential.

1. OPERATOR AND CONVENTIONS

Let G,Z be independent standard normals, e_n=He_n/sqrt(n!) the normalized
probabilists' Hermite basis, delta_Z=Z-partial_Z, and N_Z=delta_Z partial_Z.
Take 0<|lambda|<1 and a=sqrt(1-lambda^2)>0:
 X=lambda G+a Z, K=lambda, J_psi=a.
This is an exact standard Gaussian channel.

For a centered correction u=delta_Z J, the source's pointwise Newton linear
term is
 L_X(u,J)=lambda partial_G u+a partial_Z u+a J.
Because partial_G commutes with delta_Z and partial_Z delta_Z=N_Z+1,
 L_X(u,J)=[a(N_Z+2)+lambda delta_Z partial_G]J = A J.        (1)
Thus the equation for prescribed residual R is A J=-R. There is no missing
a or lambda factor, and the diagonal shift is +2.

2. EXACT CHAOS-BLOCK SOLUTION

Both N_Z and delta_Z partial_G preserve total chaos degree n. For R=e_n(G),
write
 J=sum_(j=0)^n J_j e_(n-j)(G)e_j(Z).
The recurrence is
 2a J_0=-1,
 a(j+2)J_j+lambda sqrt((n-j+1)j)J_(j-1)=0, j>=1.         (2)
Solving gives exactly
 J_j=(-1)^(j+1) a^(-1)(lambda/a)^j
             sqrt(binomial(n,j))/[(j+1)(j+2)].           (3)

For each n the block is triangular with nonzero diagonal a(j+2), hence
invertible. Formula (3) is the unique coefficient vector in that block.

3. NO BOUNDED L2 RIGHT INVERSE; STRONGER J-ONLY LOWER BOUND

The exact norm is
 ||J||_2^2=a^(-2) sum_(j=0)^n binomial(n,j)(lambda^2/a^2)^j
                                      /[(j+1)^2(j+2)^2].
Consequently
 ||J||_2 >= a^(-n-1)/[(n+1)(n+2)].                       (4)
This follows by replacing the denominator by (n+1)^2(n+2)^2 and using
1+lambda^2/a^2=a^(-2). Thus the inverse is unbounded already as an L2-to-L2
map; one need not demand a correction derivative to establish failure.

Since partial_Z u=(N_Z+1)J,
 ||partial_Z u||_2^2=a^(-2) sum_(j=0)^n
          binomial(n,j)(lambda^2/a^2)^j/(j+2)^2,
and hence
 ||partial_Z u||_2 >= a^(-n-1)/(n+2).

A FINITE VALUE REPRESENTATION OF THE AFFINE PROJECTED CORRECTION
27 October 2026. Continuation of AFFINE_NEWTON_INVERSE_AUDIT.txt.

STATUS. In d=1 the source-coupled pointwise Newton inverse is unbounded, but
its projection onto the Gaussian output admits a bounded inverse and a finite,
positive stochastic implementation with one value of the prescribed residual R.
This is NOT yet a legal g-value compiler: arbitrary Stein residual values are
not available under N687. It is a precise missing-interface construction.

1. PROJECTED INVERSE WITH SOURCE CENTERING

Let X=lambda G+aZ, Y=aG-lambda Z, a=sqrt(1-lambda^2)>0. X,Y are independent
standard normals. Gaussian derivatives and divergences rotate:
 partial_Z=a partial_X-lambda partial_Y,
 delta_Z=a delta_X-lambda delta_Y,
 partial_G=lambda partial_X+a partial_Y.
The affine pointwise Newton operator from the audit is
 A=a(N_Z+2)+lambda delta_Z partial_G
   =delta_Z partial_X+2a
   =a(N_X+2)-lambda delta_Y partial_X.                    (1)

For R in L2(gamma_2), define r(X)=E[R(G,Z)|X] and
 j(X)=-a^(-1)(N_X+2)^(-1)r(X), J=j(X), u=delta_Z J.        (2)
Then
 E[A J|X]=-r(X),     E[u|G]=0.                            (3)
The Y term in (1) has zero conditional expectation. Source-centering follows
from Gaussian divergence in Z, not merely from an unconditional mean bound.

The inverse is bounded:
 ||J||_2 <= ||r||_2/(2a) <= ||R||_2/(2a).                 (4)
Writing r=sum r_m e_m(X) gives
 u=a delta_X j-lambda Yj,
 ||u||_2^2=sum_m (a^2 m+1)|r_m|^2/[a^2(m+2)^2]
           <= ||r||_2^2/(4a^2).                         (5)
The scalar coefficient is decreasing for m>=0 when 0<a<=1, so its maximum
is 1/(4a^2). These statements extend from polynomials by L2 continuity and
weak divergence. Equation (3) is output/Stein-test projection, not pointwise
cancellation of the unprojected residual.

At an exact affine Gaussian an actual valid L2 Stein residual has r=0.
Thus (2) is a linear right inverse for prescribed projected forcing, not a
claim that an exact Gaussian needs correction. Actual nonaffine perturbations
produce nonzero first-order forcing, as the audit addendum explains.
